Exploring the workspace and Paris Open Data APIs to design an interactive Paris tree canopy explorer.


Checking API capabilities and planning the app architecture for ~220k trees.


Creating a data pipeline and building the application.


Building the application UI and core components.


**Canopée de Paris** is in `/workspace/paris-trees` — an interactive atlas of the municipal tree canopy.

### What you get
- **Map** — MapLibre on a muted Carto basemap; **Supercluster** aggregation when zoomed out; individual markers when zoomed in; color by **genre** or **height**; gold **arbres remarquables** markers; arrondissement outlines.
- **Filters** — Arrondissements 1er–20e, featured genera (Platanus, Aesculus, Tilia, Sophora, Celtis, …), height/circumference ranges, remarkable-only toggle.
- **Analytics** — Totals, diversity, mean/median height & circumference, genus bar chart, density per km² by arrondissement (updates with filters).
- **Remarkable showcase** — 182 heritage trees with photos, criteria, planting age, pan-to-map.
- **District comparison** — Stacked voirie vs parcs chart + comparison table with genus variety and density.
- **Tree detail card** — French name, taxonomy, dimensions, stade, domaine, coordinates, heritage text/PDF when available.

### Data
~220k trees from Paris Open Data, preprocessed to `public/data/trees.json.gz` (~7.4 MB download). Sources are credited in the footer.

### Run it
```bash
cd /workspace/paris-trees
npm install
npm run dev
```

Dev server: **http://localhost:5173/**

Refresh data:
```bash
npm run data:fetch
npm run data:build
```

First load parses the full inventory (brief loading screen); filtering and clustering then run in the browser on the active selection.
